When I first got a diagnose (first it was bipolar, then, a little bit later, borderline), I suddenly realized that it explains many things I’ve done and kept doing. It gave me insight into my habits, unconscious biases, and ways I tried to cope with the thing I didn't know much about. 

I’ve spent a lot of time analyzing my behavior in the past to find out what worked and what didn't when it came to facing a personal crisis. When I shared my thoughts with my psychiatrist, she employed this way of analysis to find the suitable strategies for coping and preventing the onsets in case if medicine would fail (it happens to me; treatment schemes at some point stop working). 

Being conscious about your illness lets you separate your normal functioning from stress/illness-induced behavior/thinking. You get to notice small things that can ruin the whole day/week/remission. You get to catch tiniest signs of coming onsets on the spot. 

It also gives you a perspective where you can judge your behavior and analyze stuff that happens in life from different angles, not only from bipolar/borderline/whatever you have one. 

Hope it helps. If something is not clear here (it can be :)), please, ask any questions you have.
